=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh: lines 764-767 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `unblock_py stop --labels-json` exits non-zero, the log diagnosis is always `detail=unblocked`. The `stop_for_labels` function in `unblock_ledger.py` raises `UsageError` for three distinct reasons: genuinely no block label (the common case), labels not a list (`--labels-json must be a JSON array`), or a Python-level crash. All three are logged identically, and `2>/dev/null` discards the actual error message.
  WHY: The behavior is fail-closed (the close is skipped), so no security or correctness bug. The defect is observability: an operator diagnosing a skipped terminal close cannot tell whether the item was genuinely unblocked or whether the stop resolution itself failed (e.g. a corrupted labels artifact, transient Python crash).
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh: lines ~763-770 (the `unblock_py ... stop --labels-json` failure branch) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `unblock_py "${SUPPORT_DIR}/scripts/unblock_ledger.py" stop --labels-json ...` exits non-zero, the code logs `detail=unblocked`, conflating a Python/script failure (missing script, crash, malformed labels JSON, etc.) with the genuine case where labels resolved to no block label. The only path in the file that produces this `detail` value is the command-failure path, so operators seeing `detail=unblocked` cannot tell whether labels really resolved to no block or whether the resolution itself failed.
  WHY: An operator responding to a skip alert ("judge skipped close with reason=block_state_changed detail=unblocked") would assume the item was unblocked; in reality the script may have crashed before resolving labels, leaving the item still blocked but with no actionable diagnostic. The behavioural effect remains fail-closed (skip), so this is an observability defect, not a correctness one.
